messages:
maria: FYI, during the lockfile regen last night we saw CI failures traced to tokenizers wheel incompatibility. logs show "ERROR: tokenizers-...cp39-cp39-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl is not a supported wheel" on our linux runners. possible CVE-related rebuilds upstream?

sam: ugh. which lock change pulled it in? did poetry update tokenizers or transformers?

maria: poetry.lock diff: tokenizers bumped 0.13.3 -> 0.14.0 as a transitive from transformers 4.35.0. we regen'd with `poetry lock --no-update` after changing constraints and it still pulled 0.14.0.

lee: can you paste the failing pip output? sometimes manylinux tags change and our cached wheel mirrors break.

maria: paste of relevant snippet:
```
Collecting tokenizers==0.14.0
  Downloading tokenizers-0.14.0-cp39-cp39-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl (3.2 MB)
ERROR: tokenizers-0.14.0-cp39-cp39-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl is not a supported wheel on this platform.
```

jen: that pattern usually means wheel was built for newer manylinux (musl/glibc mismatch) — our runner image is debian:buster based. Two quick fixes: 1) force-install from sdist (`pip install --no-binary :all: tokenizers==0.14.0`) or 2) pin tokenizers to 0.13.x which has compatible wheel. Both have tradeoffs.

sam: CVE angle: security team flagged tokenizers 0.13.x had a low-sev vuln but was backported/mitigated in 0.14.0 upstream. We can't ignore the CVE long term.

lee: immediate priority is unblocking CI. my vote is temporary pin to 0.13.3 in our constraints and open an incident to ship a more robust fix (rebuild runner image or add sdist fallback).

maria: agree. quick plan: 1) pin tokenizers==0.13.3 in pyproject[tool.poetry.dependencies] via a patch (not a full lock regen) and update constraints file. 2) add `pip --no-binary` fallback in our test matrix for linux to try sdist if wheel fails. 3) open a follow-up to work with infra to upgrade runners to newer manylinux-compatible images.

jen: small note — pinning 0.13.3 means we accept the low-sev CVE temporarily. security team ok with that if we create a JIRA and timeline to migrate to a patched build or verify the patch in 0.14.x?

sam: security said acceptable if we mitigate exposure: scope check (which services import tokenizers) and add runtime monitoring. also set patch priority P1 -> we need a migration within 7 days or a compensating control.

maria: created ticket INFSEC-7321 with mitigation checklist. I'll push the patch to `hotfix/tokenizers-pin` and open a PR against main with the constraint change plus CI fallback.

devops-bot: CI Pipeline #2874 failed on linux-tests (unit). See https://ci.redwood.ai/build/2874 for logs.

lee: I pushed a WIP stub to your branch to add `pip install --no-binary :all: tokenizers==0.14.0` in the matrix job as an experiment — that should confirm whether sdist build succeeds.

maria: thanks. next steps owners: maria -> push constraint pin + PR, lee -> experiment sdist fallback, jen -> confirm acceptance criteria with security (timeline), sam -> audit imports/services and list affected prod/private deployments. I'll aim to merge hotfix within the hour and then we can run full CI.

jen: adding a note: document rollback criteria in PR: if sdist installs but performance regresses (tokenizers build from source is slow), we'll accept pin until infra upgrades. :warning:

sam: 👍 also add a note to release notes and internal incident doc so oncall knows why we pinned.

maria: merged PR and kicked CI. if green, we'll cherry-pick to release branch and mark INFSEC-7321 P1 with 7d SLA. thanks all. :thumbsup:
